evidence: Test asserts patch visibility via `from rebar_reconciler import git_adapter` then `monkeypatch.setattr(git_adapter, ...)` — tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_advisory_lock.py:135-149

conftest puts the engine on sys.path and extends the package __path__: `rebar_reconciler.__path__.append(_engine_pkg)` — tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/conftest.py:81-83, and comment 'those keys resolve regardless of which object rebar_reconciler itself points at' (conftest.py:55-57), so `from rebar_reconciler import git_adapter` succeeds in this environment

lazy_load returns the already-registered module when the key is present: `if key in sys.modules: return sys.modules[key]` — src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_loader.py:54-55; so fixed and pre-fix imports converge on one object here

advisory.finding: The new test `test_git_adapter_patches_are_shared_across_package_and_by_path_loaders` runs in the package-context unit environment (conftest seeds `rebar_reconciler` importable), where the pre-fix `from rebar_reconciler import git_adapter` and the fixed `lazy_load("rebar_reconciler.git_adapter", ...)` resolve to the SAME `sys.modules["rebar_reconciler.git_adapter"]` object. The monkeypatch is therefore observed either way, so the assertions pass whether the seam carries the fix OR is reverted to the buggy absolute import — the test cannot detect the regression it purports to cover. The actual `ModuleNotFoundError` bug only manifests in the standalone by-path context (no top-level `rebar_reconciler` package), which this test never enters despite its docstring saying 'Both standalone lock seams'.
